sections.h2: Which selling routes suit a Temple Terrace homeowner?
sections.html:
Three routes cover most sales here: a listing, an investor's cash bid, or a private deal. Pick by how soon you need the money and how much work the house needs.

The city sits just outside Tampa in Hillsborough County, near the University of South Florida and the Hillsborough River. It is compact and mostly built out, so a house that is clean on title and priced sensibly draws attention quickly.

  • Listing: the biggest audience, though staging, showings and a buyer's loan add weeks.
  • Cash bid: you set the closing day, and the price usually sits below a polished listing.
  • Inherited or tenant-occupied house: who holds title, or what the lease says, sets the pace.

sections.h2: How big is Temple Terrace, and who lives in its houses?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts counts 27,075 residents on July 1, 2025, across 7.32 square miles of land. The city's own site calls it a small-town setting with urban amenities and dates the city to 1925.

Only 50.4 percent of housing units were owner-occupied in 2020 to 2024, so renters are nearly half the households (11,630 in all). Owner-occupied homes had a median value of $334,800 and rents a median of $1,594. About 80 percent of residents had not moved in the past year, which suggests plenty of long-held houses with equity in them.

sections.h2: What do income and commute numbers say about Temple Terrace buyers?
sections.html:
The city's median household income was $69,252 for 2020 to 2024, with per capita income at $38,513, and 9.0 percent of residents were in poverty, per QuickFacts. Mean travel time to work was 26.0 minutes, and 95.1 percent of households had a broadband subscription.

Those figures describe a middle-income city with moderate commutes. A buyer at that income level often needs a mortgage, so a lender's appraisal can shape a retail sale. A cash investor, by contrast, cares more about condition and rent potential than about income statistics.

  • Veterans number 1,162, a count that suggests some buyers may use VA financing.
  • Residents over 65 are 16.3 percent, a sign of long-time owners who may be downsizing.
  • About 25.7 percent of people over five speak a language other than English at home, so a bilingual listing can reach more buyers.

sections.h2: Does a guest-rental history change how a Temple Terrace house sells?
sections.html:
It can, because the city regulates guest stays through its own program. Its rules cover a home let for stays under 30 days, more than 3 times a year.

According to the city program page, those homes need a Certificate of Use renewed annually and a fire department safety inspection every two years. Each also needs a local contact on call around the clock. Breaking the rules can lead to the Municipal Code Enforcement Board and a civil citation.

  • Headcount limit: two per bedroom, plus two.
  • Parking: guest cars go on approved off-street spots only.
  • Quiet hours: 8 p.m. to 8 a.m. Sunday to Thursday, 10 p.m. to 8 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
  • Listings must display the limits, a state license number or Exempt, and the Certificate of Use number.

Before accepting an offer on a rental, pull the certificate, the latest inspection result and any citations. An investor planning to keep hosting guests will ask for that file, and the complaint hotline the page prints is 813-501-6769.

sections.h2: Which schools and nearby places help a Temple Terrace listing?
sections.html:
The schools and institutions around the city are a real selling point, and a buyer will recognize them. The city's school page lists Lewis Elementary, Riverhills Elementary and Temple Terrace Elementary, Greco Middle, and King High School in Tampa, plus private options such as Corpus Christi Catholic School and Florida College Academy.

The city's information page also points to Florida College, USF, the Museum of Science and Industry, Busch Gardens, riverfront parks, a public library, a recreation center and a historic golf and country club. Mention the ones closest to your street in your listing or your note to a buyer. Confirm school assignment with the district before you promise a particular school to anyone.

sections.h2: What does a Temple Terrace street offer a buyer?
sections.html:
The city's information page highlights riverfront parks with views of the Hillsborough River, a public library and recreation center, and a historic golf and country club. It adds that residents are minutes from USF, Florida College, the Museum of Science and Industry and Busch Gardens.

The city website also lists river navigation hazards, a River Watch Task Force, a tree adoption program and links to HART bus schedules and bicycle-friendly community information. If your house is near the river or a park, say so, and mention any trail or transit link you can see from the front door. Buyers who commute or study nearby will look for exactly that.

Walk the block before listing. Note the distance to a school from the city's list, the nearest bus stop and any city projects posted on the council agenda page, then put those facts into the listing description.

sections.h2: Which closing charges hit a Temple Terrace seller?
sections.html:
Expect a state deed tax plus clerk fees. The Department of Revenue puts the deed tax at seventy cents on each hundred dollars of price outside Miami-Dade, and says every signer of the deed is liable regardless of what the contract assigns.

The Hillsborough clerk collects the tax when the deed goes on record. Clerk fees follow section 28.24: $5.00 for page one, $4.00 for later pages, plus smaller add-ons. Have the title agent print a draft statement before you commit to a price.

  • Deed tax, due at recording.
  • Per-page clerk fees.
  • Your share of the year's property tax.

sections.h2: What happens to my tax status when a Temple Terrace house changes hands?
sections.html:
Florida's tax year starts with a January 1 valuation, and bills arrive in November with a sliding early-pay discount that begins at 4 percent. The settlement statement divides the current year's bill between you and the buyer.

Your homestead exemption stops with the sale. After a change of ownership, the buyer's valuation resets on the next January 1, so the new bill can look nothing like yours. Tell buyers to ask the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser for their own estimate.

sections.h2: What if the Temple Terrace owner is in foreclosure or settling an estate?
sections.html:
Time pressure differs in each case. A foreclosure judgment leads to a court-run sale in 20 to 35 days, and the top bidder leaves a 5 percent deposit, so a private sale beforehand is the only way to choose your buyer.

For a house left by someone who has died, Florida allows a shortened estate process when the non-exempt assets are $150,000 or less, or two years have passed since the death. A deed from a personal representative under a probated will is listed by the Department of Revenue as not taxable. Delinquent taxes bring a certificate sale, and a tax deed application can follow after two years. Consult a Florida attorney or title agent.

faqs.q: Can a Temple Terrace house close in under a month?
faqs.a: Yes, when title is clear and the buyer pays cash, closing in two or three weeks is realistic. A bank-financed buyer needs an appraisal and underwriting, which stretches the schedule.

faqs.q: Who owes the deed tax on a Temple Terrace sale?
faqs.a: The state says every party to the deed is liable, whichever one the contract names. The charge is seventy cents on each hundred dollars of price, paid to the clerk at recording.

faqs.q: I rented my house on Airbnb. What do I hand a buyer?
faqs.a: Give the buyer your Certificate of Use, the fire inspection record and any city citations. Someone who wants to keep hosting needs that registration in good standing.

faqs.q: Does my homestead break when I list the house?
faqs.a: It lasts until the sale, since it depends on the house being your permanent home and not rented out. After the sale, part of your capped assessment can follow you to a new Florida home if you claim portability within three years.
The Hillsborough County clerk of the circuit court records it, collecting the tax and per-page fees at that moment.
